correctness.rationale: For x=nk≥17, A=π(x), B=π(x+n), c=ceil(n/2), at most c odd prime candidates give Δ=B−A≤c. Therefore (k+1)log A−k log B≥log A−kc/A. Rosser–Schoenfeld’s unconditional π(x)>x/log x and monotonicity of y log y reduce sufficient positivity to 1−(log log x)/(log x)>c/n. For n≠3, c/n≤3/5 and (log log x)/(log x)<2/5 for x≥17; for n=3 use <1/3 for x≥128. Both logarithmic comparisons follow from elementary monotonic x^2/log^5 x and x/log^3 x with checked endpoints. Independently enumerated all 71 distinct remaining (n,k) with integer powers A^(k+1),B^k, finding precisely reversed (2,1),(2,2) and tie (4,1); also corroborated a larger independent sample. Thus full n≥2,k≥1 domain follows analytically plus a genuine exhaustive finite boundary.
